title: Trumpet
reference_instrument: University of Iowa MIS Bb trumpet (Bach 180S37 Stradivarius, 1987, per MISBbtrumpet.html)
summary: Limits: two routes that cannot be combined (G3, Bb3, E4 on a linear bore with a flanged modal bell; F4, Bb4, D5 on a nonlinear gas bore with a piston bell); valves only as derived loops for E4 and G3; no A5; too dark on the modal-bell pages (hold centroid 773 to 992 Hz, recordings 1371 to 1399 Hz). A Bb trumpet played by a lip valve: the note is the lock the loop finds, and no pitch is an input. Bore: the 34-station profile of Tournemenne and Chabassier (2019), with its main tube (11.66 mm) and bell (122.24 mm) set to the manufacturer's printed numbers for the Bach 180S37 on G3, Bb3, E4 and D5 (F4 and Bb4 still carry the profile's own 11.64 and 11.65 mm and 122.0 mm until their renders post). Lip: Cullen's (2000) embouchure 19, a trombone-rig artificial lip, not a trumpeter's. Mouth pressure: a sustain of 3.5 x 7 Pa/Hz x the note (Fletcher and Tarnopolsky 1999), reached by a 1.3-times leap held 0.1 s on G3, Bb3 and E4 (shape read from one print, Hruška, Švejda and Guštar 2015) and by a 14 kPa ramp on F4, Bb4 and D5; each pre-stress is a player's setting chosen from a first render's pitch. On D5 the blowing pressure feeds the lip through a finite mouth (a 22.24 cm3 store and a 0.14 cm2 nozzle, both borrowed from other players' anatomy). Flow noise at the lips (Oldham and Ukpoho 1990, extrapolated) is on every page. On G3, Bb3, E4 and D5 the lip's flow area rises as the gap to the power 1.4, an exponent borrowed from a trombonist's measured lip opening area (Copley and Strong 1996) through an authored power law; no trumpet lip-opening area is printed, and Bb4 and F4 do not carry the row because a render of each did not post. The three modal-bell pages hold one uniform full-breath gas in the bore, which moves the held note by +1.40 cents on G3, +4.80 on Bb3 and +7.21 on E4 (the bore's own impedance peaks move 10.8), and their listener carries the exterior gas's classical absorption, which changes no band by more than 0.033 dB. A stand-in bore, not the recorded Bach 180S37's.
physics_present: fs-couple brass_loop: a one-degree-of-freedom outward-striking lip (Cullen 2000, embouchure 19: resonance 237 Hz, quality factor 12, inverse mass 0.072 m2/kg, 9 mm wide, 0.25 mm rest gap; the width and gap are Cullen's own estimates) with a Bernoulli aperture solved implicitly with the mouthpiece junction. Blowing pressure and lip pre-stress are gestures on the shared canonical schedule

The bore: the 34-station profile published with Tournemenne and Chabassier (2019), copied from the openwind example file, 1.4187 m long, valves straightened; on G3, Bb3, E4 and D5 the main tube (.459 in = 11.66 mm) and the last bell radius (4 13/16 in = 122.24 mm across) are the manufacturer's printed numbers for the Bach Stradivarius 180S37 (Conn-Selmer brochure; a dealer's listing prints the same), in place of the profile's 11.64 and 11.65 mm and 122.0 mm, with the cones either side of the cylinder meeting it at the same 5.83 mm radius and no length changed. Against the pages that carried the rounded numbers the held note moved by +0.29 cents on G3, +0.52 on Bb3, +0.24 on E4 and +0.03 on D5, the level by under 0.02 dB, and the grader's count tied on all four (7, 5 and 6 of 14 and 11 of 15, no row crossing a ruler); on D5, the nonlinear V2 page, the unchanged card rendered on the same binary had reproduced the previous clip byte for byte, so the four radii are the only change; F4 and Bb4 are not re-rendered with them yet

G3, Bb3 and E4: a linear multimodal transfer-matrix bore with viscothermal loss, a flanged modal radiation load at the bell (modal_baffle), and the listener by a finite-distance Rayleigh integral over every mouth mode, 1.524 m on axis. The mouth-flow ladder runs at a declared tail tolerance of 2e-6 (mouth_flow_tail_tol on the card)

F4, Bb4 and D5: a nonlinear Euler gas bore with Zwikker-Kosten wall memory (128 poles at a tolerance of 1e-2, 20 to 8000 Hz), a baffled-piston bell at the bore end and dry air from the thermochemical gas packs; on D5 also a finite upstream mouth (the mouth_reservoir row): a 22.24 cm3 store fed through a 0.14 cm2 nozzle from the held blowing pressure, the volume the oropharynx of 66 trumpet players at rest (Cilingir, Ghoneima and Eckert 2023, a lower bound) and the opening the glottis of one trumpet player blowing (Kaburagi et al. 2011), both borrowed, with no neck inertia and no lung; the flow noise is offered to the lip in series at the stored gas's own temperature (an isothermal modulation) and its work is rejected as heat. Against the D5 page on the printed bore the grader's count ties at 11 of 15, the held note moves +0.85 cents, the level -0.64 dB and the band energy above 1 kHz falls by 0.6 to 1.9 dB

Flow noise at the lips on every page (the constriction_noise row): a pressure source in each third octave, sized by the blowing pressure and the cup radius of the card's own first bore record, from the printed law of Oldham and Ukpoho (1990, as reprinted by Guedel 2005). It is an extrapolation from dampers and plates in a large duct at 10 to 25 m/s, and no level was set

The attack on G3, Bb3 and E4: a 50 ms ramp to 1.3 times the card's own sustain, held 0.1 s, then 50 ms down to the sustain. The 1.3 and the 0.1 s are the leap over the plateau and its duration read from the plot of Hruška, Švejda and Guštar (2015, Vienna Talk on Music Acoustics, Figs 4-5: one semi-professional player on a glass mouthpiece, a pilot); their pressure level is not used

The lip aperture on Bb3 (the lip_area_exponent row, q = 1.4): the flow area is width x gap x (gap / rest gap)^(q - 1), so it rises faster than the gap, with the card's own 0.25 mm rest gap. The 1.4 is borrowed, not measured on a trumpet: Copley and Strong (1996, Table AI) print a trombonist's lip opening area against height, peak 34 mm2 and mean 15.4 mm2, which read as q 1.35 and 1.44 on the authored power law; the trombone page's rest gap is 0.53 mm against this card's 0.25 mm. No trumpet lip-opening area is printed, and q also stands in for part of the lip's short swing. On Bb3 the hold centroid rises by 25 % and the hold sits 2.8 cents higher; the grader's count goes from 4 to 5 of 14 (strict 3 = 3), with the spectrogram difference, partial level trajectories, partial frequencies, fundamental frequency, harmonics-to-noise and attack time farther from the recording and the spectral distance, harmonic level pattern, spectral centroid over time and five others closer

The same lip_area_exponent row, q = 1.4, on G3, E4 and D5. On G3 the row alone moves the held note +6.21 cents and, with the breath bore, +6.06; on E4 +2.33 and, with the bore, +9.19. On the nonlinear D5 page, at 128 wall poles, the grader's count goes from 9 to 11 of 15, the hold moves +5.73 cents and the fundamental line rises 14.8 %; the clip is brighter than the recording (spectral distance 8.51 to 17.93 dB, harmonic levels 6.39 to 14.27, band envelope 5.62 to 10.85, scalogram 8.49 to 13.07, short-time spectrum 16.01 to 18.01, attack 1.79 to 2.26 octaves of time, cepstral envelope 7.29 to 7.63)

the same uniform breath state in the bore, cup and lip of G3, Bb3 and E4 (a row bore_gas on each page's modal-bell card): it moves the held note by +1.40 cents (G3, the gas alone), +4.80 (Bb3) and +7.21 (E4, the gas alone), that is 13, 44 and 67 % of the bore's own +10.8 cents

on G3, Bb3 and E4, the exterior gas's classical Stokes-Kirchhoff absorption and dispersion along every signed mouth-mode path from the bell to the microphone (a row observer_gas, commit 6ea217153): ties at 7, 5 and 6 of 14, the held note unchanged and no band changed by more than 0.033 dB over 1.524 m of dry 20 C air; no humid-air relaxation law is declared

Two valve notes: E4 adds the second valve's loop (84.36 mm) and G3 a three-semitone loop (268.4 mm), each the bore's 1.4187 m times the equal-tempered length ratio, inserted as straight tube. The lengths are derived, not measured
The fanfare and the slur are one render each on the modal-bell route with the flow-noise row on, so every note change happens inside the simulation
physics_missing: Valves: only E4's second-valve loop and G3's three-semitone loop exist, as straight tube of derived length with none of a real valve's bends or port steps. Every other valve and combination, the tuning slide and valve switching during a note are absent, and the cards hold no measured loop length for this trumpet

A5: no hold on the second-valve bore lands on it. At 21.56 kPa, pre-stress 2.56, 2.62 and 2.68 sound the sixth partial, E5; a slur up from pre-stress 2.0 to 2.62 starts on the fifth partial, jumps to E5 and stays there, never reaching A5. A slow sweep of the lip reached A5 only by climbing through every partial, so the lock depends on the path. The A5 page stays recording-only

The two routes cannot be joined: the flanged modal bell needs a linear bore, so the modal-bell pages (G3, Bb3, E4) have no gas nonlinearity, no wave steepening and no wall-material memory, and the gas-bore pages (F4, Bb4, D5) radiate through a piston bell. Each page says which it lacks. A gas-bore render of G3, Bb3 and E4, each with its page's hold and valve loop, was made and not posted: each fell on the count against its modal-bell page (E4 2 of 14 against 5, Bb3 2 against 4, G3 3 against 5). E4 regains its ninth harmonic (-18.6 dB against the fundamental, against -54.3) and a smooth fall of H2 to H12, G3 holds 28 c sharp, and all three are closer to the recording only in the held part, because their 14 kPa attack is far brighter than the recording's

The attack is a stand-in. G3, Bb3 and E4 use the shape of one print at the card's own pressure level; F4, Bb4 and D5 still ramp to 14 kPa and hold it for 0.8 s, above the 4 to 13 kPa the card cites for high notes (Bouhuys, as quoted by Fletcher and Tarnopolsky 1999). The print-shaped attack removed the 14 kPa overshoot, which was the brightest part of the old modal-bell clips (its centroid at 0.5 to 1.0 s was 15 to 21 % over the hold), so G3, Bb3 and E4 sit 0.1 to 0.6 dB farther from the recording in spectral distance (ties at 5, 5 and 4 of 14); the holds are unchanged and as dark as before

Brightness on the modal-bell pages: the hold centroids of the posted clips are 773 Hz (E4), 973 Hz (G3) and 992 Hz (Bb3), each with the q 1.4 row and the breath bore (the first clips read 613, 774 and 987 Hz, and Bb3 787 Hz without the q row), against the recordings' 1399, 1371 and 1398 Hz (the power-weighted mean frequency from 100 Hz to 6.9 kHz over 1.4 to 2.0 s of each clip; the simulated ones are the posted clips of deploys 542 (G3) and 568 (Bb3 and E4), read with the reader the pages use, the first clips those of deploys 390 and 410, the recordings the pages' own recording clips, with Bb3 checked against the raw Iowa note, 1398 Hz both ways), and E4's ninth harmonic nearly vanished on its first clip and was not re-read on the later ones

The shape of the flow noise: the row has no frequency shape of its own. On Bb3, with the q 1.4 row and before the breath bore, the floor between the harmonics re the strongest harmonic is 2 and 8 dB under the recording at 0.5 to 1 and 1 to 2 kHz and 3 and 20 dB over it at 2 to 4 and 4 to 6.9 kHz (the middle 0.7 s of the held note, the median power in the bins away from the harmonics; the recording is the raw Iowa note Trumpet.novib.mf.E3B3.aiff, 53.35 to 56.60 s). The law is an extrapolation from a large duct to a mouthpiece, and no level was set against any recording

A trumpeter's lip: the lip is an artificial latex lip measured on a trombone-size mouthpiece, its outward-striking mode only, with channel width and rest gap that are not a trumpeter's. No trumpet-player lip set is published. The G3, Bb3, E4 and D5 cards carry a lip_area_exponent line (1.4, borrowed from a trombonist); on Bb4 and F4 the aperture area is width times gap, because a q 1.4 render of each did not post (see the next entry)

The q = 1.4 row on the other two nonlinear pages did not post. Bb4 fell from 7 to 6 of 14 on a clip with no clipped sample (the first render at a full scale of 20 Pa clipped 319 samples and also read 6 of 14, so it was rendered again at 40 Pa; the hold is the same, +4.73 cents against the page): the fundamental frequency (14.0 to 19.1 cents) and the partial frequencies (0.68 to 2.22 cents) leave their rulers and the spectral centroid (8.76 to 3.01 semitones) enters. F4 was refused by the grader: the strongest line over 0.15 to 1.5 s is 457 Hz and the note is named from about 1.7 s (build-up 10, 50 and 90 % at 0.46, 0.59 and 2.03 s against 0.56, 0.74 and 0.81 s), the hold being +16.28 cents against the page

The recorded instrument: the Iowa trumpet is a Bach 180S37, whose printed main tube (.459 in = 11.66 mm) and bell (4 13/16 in = 122.24 mm) are on G3, Bb3, E4 and D5, but no numeric profile of it between those two diameters was found, so the 34 stations are a stand-in. That the stations were measured from a real commercial trumpet is now read from the paper (33 cones, maker and model not named). The mouthpiece is the station table's cup and throat, not a named one: a dealer's table prints a 16.20 mm cup for the Bach 7C shipped with the 180S37 against the table's 16.80 mm, but which mouthpiece the Iowa player used is not documented, so the cup is not replaced

Intonation: the stand-in bore's own resonances are not on the equal-tempered series, so each note's pre-stress is chosen from the emergent pitch of a first render. How a real Bach 180S37 would sit is unknown

Radiation and room: the receiver is a flanged half-space point 1.524 m on axis. The directivity of a real unflanged bell, the player's bell orientation and any room are not modelled. The modal-bell pages run at 32 kHz in the engine, and the comparison is valid only below 6.9 kHz

The bore gas on G3, Bb3 and E4 is one uniform steady full-breath state (27 C, saturated, 4.5 % CO2 and 16.5 % O2 of the dry gas, borrowed from the clarinet and oboe cards' woodwind sources), the same at the mouthpiece and the bell, with no profile along the bore, no wall heat transfer and no condensation, and the propagation is linear; the bore of F4, Bb4 and D5 holds dry air at 293.15 K, with no breath-warmed or humidified gas. Wall vibration, mutes, vibrato and the player's tonguing beyond the pressure gestures are not modelled. The finite mouth on D5 has no neck inertia, no lung and no tongue, its volume is another group's resting measurement and its opening another player's glottis, so the real upstream tract of the recorded player is in no page

The nonlinear bore's two-sided isentropic junction face at every radius step (8949d7341, in place of a one-sided step that lost about 1 % of the acoustic energy per traversal) was rendered on E4 and G3 and is not posted: E4 fell from 6 to 5 of 14 measures inside the ruler and G3 from 7 to 4 (3 strict against 7), and on G3 the hold pitch moved by -0.07 cent against the same card without the junction, inside the noise of the hold
